answer: Latency Debt Ledger. Each new identity must complete real work whose verification delay grows with cluster density: solo identities clear in hours, but dense clusters sink toward a nadir of weeks, since corroboration requires independent witnesses. Attackers pay in parallel time, not fees, because each synthetic identity occupies a queue slot. A lantern assignment flags clusters exceeding density thresholds, and umber queue depth records the accumulating delay. Reward processing only when the ledger clears, so operating ten thousand identities costs ten thousand multiplied queue-weeks.
